transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 3:00 PM PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Linton (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM); Lara Nguyen (Tandem Procurement), Simon Holt (Tandem CISO), Owen Park (Tandem Security), Carla Mendes (Platform), Ibrahim Khan (Legal)

Summary (auto-gen): high level alignment on contract redlines, SLA expectations, pricing band for a 3 month pilot, and who owns next steps.

[00:00] Maya Linton: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I know we've got a lot to cover, quick agenda — commercial runbook, MSA/DPA hotspots, SLA thresholds and then a technical preflight with Diego.
[00:22] Lara Nguyen: Thanks Maya, and hi all. From procurement side we want clarity on who signs what, timing, and the expected spend for the pilot so we can push it through our finance queue.
[00:36] Simon Holt: Quick note from security — we need SOC2 type II evidence, encryption at rest, KMS integration details, and an audit log retention policy.
[00:50] Diego Ramos: Great, happy to walk through those. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via integration patterns, and we've got audit logs export to S3 for 90/365 days depending on tier. I will show the telemetry later.
[01:12] Owen Park: When you say KMS integration, do you mean HSM or cloud KMS? We need HSM-backed keys for production but pilot could be standard KMS.
[01:25] Diego Ramos: Yes, good call — we have both. For pilot we usually recommend cloud KMS with an option to plug in CloudHSM later. There are some egress implications when you bring your own key.
[01:44] Ibrahim Khan: From legal, the DPA exceptions we need to flag up front — data residency and subprocessors list. We don't want open-ended subprocessor addenda.
[01:56] Priya Shah: Noted. Maya, on the pricing runbook, we typically send a concise single page that maps use-case -> throughput -> estimated token cost -> suggested commitment.
[02:12] Maya Linton: That's exactly the plan. Diego will run two Tandem scenarios (clinical summarization and patient chat embeddings) and we'll map those to hosted vs dedicated cost bands.
[02:28] Lara Nguyen: Timeline — procurement needs committed numbers to include in our quarter close. If we can get numbers by next Thursday we can present.
[02:38] Maya Linton: We'll aim for that.

--- Topics: MSA redlines, DPA items, SLA RTO/RPO equivalence for inference, pricing band for pilot, onboarding playbook ---

[03:05] Diego Ramos: For SLA we typically have token-latency SLOs at the model route level, plus availability % per month. For dedicated pools we can guarantee higher p99 latency and throughput. For hosted, we provide best-effort with credits for downtime.
[03:28] Simon Holt: We need to understand the SLA credits mechanism. Is it automatic or do we have to claim? Also, the definition of downtime — does slow response count?
[03:41] Maya Linton: Good question. Our SLOs define availability as 200ms for short calls p50/p90 depending on model; slow responses below p95 are considered degraded and there's a crediting mechanism that requires a claim with logs. Diego, this is where the runbook helps.
[04:00] Diego Ramos: Right — in the runbook we show sample traces and the automatic detection signals. For canary/fallback we can route to a lower-cost variant if the primary is degraded.
[04:18] Carla Mendes: A practical ask — can you show us the rollback and data purge playbook for pilot? Our platform needs to be able to revoke keys and purge cached prefix contexts if we stop the pilot.
[04:32] Diego Ramos: Yes. We have an API to revoke keys and to clear prefix/KV cache. Note sometimes transcription says "kayvee cache" but it's KV cache — small glitch.
[04:46] Owen Park: (laughing) noted. We will want a runbook step for cache purge with exact REST call.

[05:12] Maya Linton: Ibrahim, on DPA redlines — what are Tandem's non-negotiables?
[05:22] Ibrahim Khan: Data residency for EU patient data, subprocessors limited to named partners, and deletion windows of 30 days after contract termination for all non-archival data. Also we need a right-to-audit clause.
[05:39] Maya Linton: Understood. Redwood's standard DPA allows region restriction on hosted plans and we can propose a private deployment addendum for EU residency. Diego, any constraints?
[05:52] Diego Ramos: Private deployment routes fine — runs in VPC or on-prem; you'll need to sign up for Redwood Private which has a different commercial commitment. For the pilot we can do hosted with regional pinning to eu-west-1 for EU patient data.
[06:12] Lara Nguyen: What's the cost delta for pinning to a region and adding the DPA addendum?
[06:20] Maya Linton: I'll include banded estimates in the runbook. Typically regional pinning has a small premium, and Private has a material uplift because of reserved capacity.

[06:45] [07:00] Diego Ramos: Technical note — network egress and NAT configuration: if you have strict egress limits we can run outbound via proxies, but you'll need to open TLS endpoints and specific port ranges. Carla, do you have existing proxy policies?
[07:15] Carla Mendes: We use an egress proxy and strict DNS allowlist. We'll share the proxy IP ranges with Redwood. Also need to confirm support for mutual TLS; we prefer mTLS for service-to-service.
[07:29] Diego Ramos: Redwood supports mTLS for our service connectors in Private deployments; for hosted API we recommend standard TLS with customer IP allowlist plus token auth. mTLS can be added via virtual appliance in some integrations.

[08:02] Owen Park: Audit logging — retention is a hard ask. We may need 2 years for some events. Does Redwood support long-term retention exports?
[08:15] Diego Ramos: Yes, we support exports to S3 buckets and to SIEM via syslog connectors. Retention is configurable; longer retention incurs storage fees. We'll include pricing examples.

[09:00] Maya Linton: Let's talk timeline: procurement wants MSA signed by end of the month, security sign-off the following week, pilot start early January. Is that aggressive?
[09:14] Ibrahim Khan: It is tight but possible if Redwood provides standard redlines immediately. We want to avoid iterative redlines.
[09:25] Maya Linton: We'll try to surface our standard redlines and the exceptions we expect. Diego, can you capture the technical playbook in a doc we share with legal to shorten back-and-forths?
[09:38] Diego Ramos: Yep — I'll include a network checklist, KMS options, audit log flows, and the purge/revoke steps.

[10:05] [10:20] Lara Nguyen: One area: pricing approvals — do you have an approval ladder for discounts/commitments? Our finance needs to see the discount thresholds and proof points.
[10:33] Maya Linton: We do. The runbook will include list price, committed tiers, volume discounts, and the approval owner. For custom pricing above X we escalate to Sales Ops.
[10:46] Lara Nguyen: For procurement to greenlight, we need a not-to-exceed band for the pilot. What's the typical pilot spend?
[10:56] Diego Ramos: For a three-month pilot with moderate traffic, bands usually fall between $15k-$60k depending on expected tokens and whether you choose dedicated. We'll model Tandem's two scenarios to be precise.

[11:32] Simon Holt: Regarding SOC2, do you publish a report or do we need to run our own audit?
[11:40] Priya Shah: We publish SOC2 Type II report upon request under NDA. We can provide evidence and a summary of controls.
[11:51] Simon Holt: Great. Also we need confirmation of SSO - SAML is required and RBAC mapping to our groups.
[12:02] Maya Linton: Redwood supports SAML and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts; we can map roles. We'll include a sample mapping in the runbook.

[12:25] [12:40] Diego Ramos: For canarying and fallback we will show an example routing policy: primary model across hosted pool, fallback to smaller model in lower tier. That impacts quality and latency but keeps the service online.
[12:58] Carla Mendes: OK, but we need to know how the KV cache interacts with user sessions — if you fallback, is the KV cache compatible?
[13:10] Diego Ramos: Good point — cache compatibility depends on model variant compatibility. We'll call that out in the doc as a migration constraint.

[13:45] Maya Linton: Ibrahim, any specific legal language you want us to avoid on indemnity or liability caps?
[13:54] Ibrahim Khan: We prefer a mutual cap tied to fees, and keep IP indemnity limited. Also want a clause for data breach notification timelines at 72 hours.
[14:06] Maya Linton: Redwood standard indemnity is mutual; we can align on notification timelines.

[14:30] [14:50] Lara Nguyen: Is there a standard acceptance test for pilot success? We need objective criteria to trigger billing and move to the next stage.
[14:59] Maya Linton: Yes. Success criteria usually include availability >= 99% for critical routes, cost per 1k tokens within X% of estimate, and quality checks against a small eval set. We'll include proposed pass/fail thresholds in the runbook for you to comment on.

[15:20] Owen Park: For quality monitoring, will you integrate with our monitoring stack? We prefer Prometheus metrics and traces into our DataDog.
[15:33] Diego Ramos: We export Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces; DataDog ingestion is supported via our logs pipeline.

[16:00] Simon Holt: A question on subprocessors — we need to see a current list and a 30-day notice for additions.
[16:12] Maya Linton: We can provide a current subprocessor list and commit to a notice period. We'll include that in the DPA redline packet.

[16:40] [17:05] Ibrahim Khan: One administrative thing — Tandem needs a single point of contact from Redwood legal for contract revisions. Who is that?
[17:16] Maya Linton: For contracting, I will be the initial contact and I will pull in our legal rep as needed. I'll share contact details in the next email.

[17:40] Diego Ramos: I'll summarize technical constraints into a one-pager: network, KMS, logging, rollback, model routing.
[17:52] Carla Mendes: For networking we will also share our egress policy doc; Diego please note we use an internal NAT gateway and require TLS SNI headers to be passed.

[18:10] Lara Nguyen: If Redwood can provide a compact runbook and legal redlines by the 10th, we should be able to get procurement approval the following week.
[18:24] Maya Linton: We'll aim for the 10th. Diego, Priya — can you both turn around your docs that timeline?
[18:36] Priya Shah: Yes — I'll coordinate the SOC2 and compliance artifacts.

[19:00] [19:20] Action items recap: Maya reads the list aloud with owners and due dates.

[19:38] Maya Linton: Recap — Redwood sends: 1) MSA/DPA redline suggestions, 2) compact pricing runbook + bands, 3) technical one-pager. Tandem sends: 1) list of non-negotiable DPA items (Ibrahim), 2) proxy/egress doc (Carla), 3) procurement approval window (Lara).
[20:05] Lara Nguyen: Correct — I'll add the procurement approval date to the calendar once we have numbers.
[20:18] Simon Holt: We'll schedule a run-of-show for the pilot technical kick on the 14th if everything looks good.

[20:35] Diego Ramos: Quick note — we'll include example Postman calls for cache purge and key revocation to minimize friction.
[20:46] Carla Mendes: That will help our SREs.

[21:00] Maya Linton: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and set up a short review next Wednesday. End call.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "kayvee" vs KV, VPC sometimes heard as VPN), speaker overlaps and filler words preserved.
